exp-1f137c273ec6.approach: Keep enlarged Audiveris melody recognition fixed and add a conservative image-derived chord-text recognition and structured harmony conversion stage.
exp-1f137c273ec6.objective: On the seven first-per-song pilot excerpts, recover missing printed chord symbols from the region above the staff using enlarged-image OCR and a strict chord grammar. Convert roots, qualities, explicit extensions and slash basses into a parseable editable kern harmony spine. Preserve existing melody events; record chord bounding boxes and proposed onset alignment separately, marking ambiguous timing for review. Do not infer absent symbols from musical plausibility or consult references.
exp-1f137c273ec6.success_criteria: Produce sealed parseable predictions for all seven pilot images, source code and per-image diagnostics distinguishing OCR failures, unsupported chord syntax and uncertain onset alignment. Compare protected chord edit error and matches with enlarged Audiveris baseline (30/38 errors, 8 matches), and verify melody error does not increase from 87/130 errors. Include round-trip parse checks and synthetic transposition checks for melody, chord roots and slash basses; distinguish these checks from measured transcription correctness. Report timing as unaudited.

exp-d6d6755b413e.approach: Retain the parent's image-derived chord OCR and replace its unavailable-baseline dependency with fresh enlarged-image melody recognition and validated kern serialization.
exp-d6d6755b413e.objective: On the same seven pilot images, first inspect the parent serializer and determine why protected evaluation found zero parseable outputs despite its local checks. Run Audiveris on enlarged images in this container, installing required dependencies within the worker budget, and convert actual recognized melody into kern. Integrate the existing chord OCR without changing its recognition thresholds. Do not assume prior baseline artifacts exist, substitute dummy melody, or infer missing notes from musical plausibility. Validate complete files with an independent kern reader and report explicit failures if recognition or conversion cannot be completed. Preserve chord bounding boxes and flag onset alignment as unaudited.
exp-d6d6755b413e.success_criteria: Submit sealed predictions and per-image recognition, conversion and independent parsing diagnostics for all seven inputs. Target seven parseable files and melody error no worse than the enlarged Audiveris baseline of 87/130 errors. Compare protected chord error against both the parent's 25/38 errors and baseline's 30/38; report any regressions rather than assuming OCR gains survive integration. Test upward-major-second transposition on actual generated melody, chord roots and slash basses, separating structural checks from transcription correctness. Retain raw recognition outputs and document missing dependencies or runtime limits.
exp-d6d6755b413e.delta_note: Negative is improvement; same fixed sample scope. Not held-out evidence.

exp-ee56f2b32016.approach: Repair the documented Java/native-library startup failure with a bounded single-image Audiveris preflight before rerunning the existing integration pipeline.
exp-ee56f2b32016.objective: Inspect inherited recognition-command diagnostics and capture the exact startup exception. Correct only the implicated Java runtime or native-library dependency; retain the existing chord OCR thresholds and melody conversion. Spend at most 180 seconds establishing a real MusicXML export from one pilot image. If that succeeds, process all seven pilot images and independently parse each complete generated kern file, repairing serialization only where an actual parser diagnostic identifies a defect. If preflight fails, stop and retain the exact commands, runtime versions and exception rather than generating placeholder transcriptions. Never consult references or invent missing notes. Preserve raw recognition and chord bounding boxes; keep chord timing explicitly unaudited.
exp-ee56f2b32016.success_criteria: Deliver reproducible startup diagnostics and a real single-image MusicXML export as the first milestone. Then target seven independently parseable sealed predictions. Protected evaluation must compare melody error with the enlarged Audiveris baseline of 87/130 and both evaluated parents' 1.0 error; compare chord error with the earlier OCR parent's 25/38, the immediate parent's 38/38 and baseline's 30/38. Check upward-major-second transposition on actual generated notes, chord roots and slash basses, reporting untested cases separately. Successful startup or parsing alone must not be called musical correctness.

exp-431cde96831a.approach: Install the specifically missing GTK 3 runtime and verify native-library resolution before a bounded Audiveris export preflight.
exp-431cde96831a.objective: Reproduce the inherited gtk-3 loading failure, install the distribution's GTK 3 runtime package and verify libgtk-3 resolves, recording package names and runtime versions. Retain Java 25 and Audiveris 5.11 plus unchanged OCR thresholds and melody conversion. Within 240 seconds obtain a genuine MusicXML export from one pilot image; stop with exact diagnostics if this fails. If successful, run the existing pipeline on all seven pilot images, independently validate complete kern outputs, and repair only parser-confirmed serialization defects. Preserve raw recognition outputs and chord bounding boxes. Do not fabricate notes or use references; mark chord timing unaudited.
exp-431cde96831a.success_criteria: Deliver native-library verification and either a real single-image MusicXML export or a reproducible failure report. If preflight succeeds, submit seven sealed predictions with per-image parsing diagnostics and actual-output upward-major-second transposition checks for melody, chord roots and slash basses. Protected evaluation should compare parseability against 0/7, melody errors against baseline 87/130 and prior experiments' 1.0 rate, and chord errors against the best experiment's 25/38 and baseline 30/38. Report regressions and untested cases explicitly; startup, parsing and synthetic checks do not establish musical correctness.
